reviews.report:
REVIEW RECORD, rules/csharp-quality/language.md (CS-LANG), phase 8, 2026-10-11. Toolchain: pinned run.sh, SDK 10.0.401, net8.0;net10.0. Fixtures: .cache/research-lang/dotnet-tools/fixtures/review-language/ (red/, green/, cells/, held/, probe/, li/, rv/, gh/, bc/, fd/).

VERDICT: no blocker. The file is faithful to the consolidation (see 2) and its cells are mechanically sound. 38 of 38 cells ran verbatim (extracted from the fenced blocks by script). On the planted red tree 38/38 printed their violation, and on the green twin 37/37 printed nothing (L09 prints 1 by design). No cell errored and none uses a placeholder. Weakness is precision and reach: 13 cells have a measured false positive or miss on probes or real trees. One real contradiction with a sibling (CS-LANG-10 against CS-PROC-18) and one false rationale (CS-LANG-23, prose headers) need fixing before ship.

1. VERIFICATION HONESTY
Cells in the unit: L01a, L01b, L02, L03a, L03b, L03c, L05a, L05b, L06, L07, L08, L09, L10a, L10b, L10c, L11a, L11b, L11c, L12, L13, L15a, L15b, L16, L18, L19, L20, L21a, L21b, L22a, L22b, L23a, L23b, L23c, L23d, L24a, L24b, L24c, L25.
Red/green mechanics: all red hits as the Verification cells state, all green clean (git repo for L23d, dotnet msbuild for L01a, L09, L16). The shipped analyzers.editorconfig, analyzers.globalconfig and BannedSymbols.txt also pass L03a, L05a, L08, L21a, L22a and L24a-c, so the unit is coherent with dotnet-build/checks.
Build claims spot-checked (shipped config, net8.0 and net10.0): CA1062 on an unguarded public dereference, IDE0370 on a dead `!`, IDE0010 and IDE0072 despite a discard arm, CS4012, CS4007, CA2014, CS9258 and CS9264 all fire as stated. RS0030 on `a.Reverse()` is red on net8.0 only (CA1806 muted) as stated. Not re-run: CS9273 vs CS9272, MA0143, RS0016 entry texts, the C# 15 and RC1 rows.
Real trees (restsharp, opentelemetry-dotnet, NLog, kiota-dotnet, grpc-dotnet; hits per repo in held/): L06 precise (0 FP of 1,504 hits). L03b is true-positive-dominated but 18 of 436 hits (NLog 6 of 14) are `!` in strings or comments. L10b: 4 of 5 hits are the word "unsafe" in comments. L10c: 2 of 4 hits are `<AllowUnsafeBlocks>false`. L21b: 4 of 4 NLog hits are plain casts, not collection expressions. L25: RestSharp flags 24 of 127 src files, all legitimate hand-split partial extension classes; NLog adds T4 and legacy splits. L22b: 1 hit, a true fail-open (otel Prometheus `_ => true`). L23a and L23b hits are true by the rule (vendored `<auto-generated/>` shims, *.Designer.cs). L11b `field ??=` hits (otel, 11) are the read-each-hit kind. L12, L13 and L20 had zero hits in these corpora; their misses are probe-verified only. L10a and L12 need PublicAPI files, which these trees mostly lack.
Probe-verified defects: L08 passes with the ban commented out; L02 misses a multi-line NoWarn and WarningsNotAsErrors; L05b misses `new System.ArgumentNullException(`; L11a misses `private readonly int field`, `public static int field`, `int field;`; L10b misses a signature split over two lines; L19 does not look in props or csproj for `<NoWarn>CS9124`; L03b passes `default!` with a trailing `// null-forgiving:` comment although the rule says never; L22b flags `Where(_ => true)`; L20 misses `public partial record struct` and `file record struct`. L05a, L21a and others print only a stderr line when .globalconfig or .editorconfig is missing, so stdout is vacuously empty.

2. FIDELITY
Rules 01-13, 15, 16, 18-25 match the consolidation in meaning and severity (MUST except 07, 13, 22, 25 = SHOULD, as in the source). IDs are stable. CS-LANG-14 and 17 are marked "retired, not reused" in the Dates bullet, and dotnet-upgrade/references/re-checks.md carries the CS-LANG-17 re-check. The netstandard2.0 conditional section is reduced to one reach line (note N-1). Additions beyond the consolidation (the L11a `{`, CS9258 and CS9264 L11c, CS-LANG-24 table measurements) are measured and sound. The one unfaithful item is a rationale that over-claims (finding F2).

3. CONTRADICTIONS
Confirmed: CS-LANG-10 and L10c ban `AllowUnsafeBlocks` everywhere, but CS-PROC-18 mandates `[LibraryImport("libc", EntryPoint="kill")]`, which does not build without it (SYSLIB1062 plus CS0227 on both TFMs; with it on, CA5392 is the next error). The processes author fixture sets AllowUnsafeBlocks in its green project, yet processes.md never says so (F1). Soft: CS-PERF-04 says "take a ReadOnlySpan<T> parameter" without "internal", against CS-LANG-10's no span in public signatures (F12). No conflict found for: CA1062 vs CS-BUILD-12 and CS-TEST-12 (consistent), guard-faults-the-Task vs CS-ERR (consistent), PERF-03 `partial` vs LANG-25 (consistent), LANG-03 vs JSON-08 and API-17, LANG-21 vs PERF-04, MA0143 vs BUILD-15 (MeziantouAnalysisMode None).

4. DELETION TEST
CS-LANG-13 (compound assignment operators): zero hits in 5 mature repos, no agent tendency evidenced, 2-line niche; delete candidate. CS-LANG-25 (partial): an agent does not add `partial` unprompted and the cell is FP-heavy; delete or cut to a reading note (cited by CS-PERF-03, so keep the ID's meaning or edit that row). CS-LANG-02's NoWarn half repeats CS-BUILD-12 ("no analyzer ID in NoWarn") and the CS-CORE-01 weaken list; the WarningsAsErrors-by-list half is unique. L10b's async-span half repeats CS4012 and CS4007, which are compile errors; only the `unsafe` half is unique. CS-LANG-09 half repeats the CS-BUILD-01 grep, and its other half ("every behavioural test runs on every TFM") has no check.

5. ERA AND PORTABILITY
No /home/ paths, no ocx, Ocx or research-host names, no [CL]/[NUL] keys in the file. Versions and the 2026-10-11 date are present on every measured claim. Gaps (F16): corpus counts (221/562 directives, 1,130 primary constructors, 2,155 vs 1,401, 2,316 and 2,028 generated, 407 vs 12,483, 8 repos, 15/7 repos) are never tied to a named corpus or date in the rows; two external attributions are undated ("The runtime team's guidance", "Roslyn calls net8.0 with C# 14 an unsupported configuration"); line 33 says "owner default 1" while the index calls it D1 under "Owner Defaults".

6. READING
Imperative, no hedging found. TOC present (204 lines) and all 7 anchors resolve. Frontmatter matches siblings. Rows run long: mean 926 chars, max 1,703 (CS-LANG-05), against rule-distillation's "Rationale: one line"; the measurement logs in the Verification cells of 03, 05, 11, 12, 19 and 24 are the bulk (F15). Trigger: see trigger_eval.

FINDINGS are in the structured list; F1 and F2 should be fixed before ship, the rest are cell hardening.

findings.problem: CS-LANG-10 and cell L10c forbid AllowUnsafeBlocks everywhere, but CS-PROC-18 mandates a [LibraryImport("libc", EntryPoint="kill")] import and CS-LANG-25 lists [LibraryImport] as a legitimate generator. LibraryImport does not compile without AllowUnsafeBlocks, so following both rules is impossible.
findings.evidence: li/ fixture: net8.0;net10.0, AnalysisLevel 10.0-all, K.cs with the CS-PROC-18 import. Without the property: SYSLIB1062 'LibraryImportAttribute requires unsafe code' plus CS0227 on both TFMs (4 errors). With <AllowUnsafeBlocks>true</AllowUnsafeBlocks> the next error is CA5392. The author-processes green fixture's Engine.csproj sets AllowUnsafeBlocks=true; rules/csharp-quality/processes.md never mentions it.
findings.fix: Reword the tail of CS-LANG-10 to: 'No `unsafe` keyword. No AllowUnsafeBlocks except in the one project that holds the CS-PROC-18 LibraryImport.' Change L10c to print every AllowUnsafeBlocks set to true (pattern 'AllowUnsafeBlocks>[[:space:]]*true') and say in the cell that exactly the LibraryImport project may appear. In processes.md CS-PROC-18 add 'that project sets AllowUnsafeBlocks (SYSLIB1062) and a DefaultDllImportSearchPaths attribute (CA5392)'.

findings.problem: CS-LANG-23's rationale says any listed marker 'skips the file in every analyzer', and the Gate-blinding class repeats it. A prose '// File generated from ...' header does not skip analysis; only the <auto-generated / <autogenerated comment, the *.g.cs / *.generated.cs / *.designer.cs name and [GeneratedCode] do. Cell L23a's prose alternative is also case-sensitive, so 'Generated by' and 'Code generated by' headers are missed.
findings.evidence: gh/ fixture, SDK 10.0.401, net10.0, AnalysisLevel 10.0-all, a CA1305 plus CA1812 trigger in each file. Skipped (no diagnostics): '// <auto-generated/>', '// <autogenerated>', Foo.g.cs, Foo.generated.cs, Foo.designer.cs, [GeneratedCode]. Analyzed (errors reported): '// Generated by tool', '// File generated from spec', '// This file was generated by X', '// Code generated by protoc', '// This file is auto-generated', '/* auto-generated */'. Probe: L23a reported MISS for '// Generated by tool', '// Generated from spec', '// This file was generated by X' and 'Code generated by'.
findings.fix: Rewrite the Rule and Rationale: three analyzer-skipping markers (comment containing <auto-generated or <autogenerated, the three file-name suffixes, [GeneratedCode]); the prose header is banned as mimicry only ('analyzers still run on it, measured 2026-10-11'). Make L23a case-insensitive for the prose alternative (grep -rliE ... -e '^//[[:space:]]*(file )?(this file was )?generated (by|from)'). Adjust the Gate-blinding row wording.

findings.problem: Cell L08 counts lines containing 'MemoryExtensions.Reverse' in BannedSymbols.txt, so a commented-out or malformed ban line still prints nothing while the RS0030 ban is inert and the net8.0 miscompile is back.
findings.evidence: rv/ fixture: ban line live -> net8.0 build error RS0030, L08 silent. Prefixing the line with '// ' -> build 0 errors on both TFMs, and 'grep -c MemoryExtensions.Reverse BannedSymbols.txt | grep -vx 1' still prints nothing (count 1).
findings.fix: Anchor the pattern: grep -c '^M:System\.MemoryExtensions\.Reverse``1(System\.Span{``0})' BannedSymbols.txt | grep -vx 1. State in the cell that registering the file as AdditionalFiles is CS-BUILD-15's check.

findings.problem: L02 only sees single-line <WarningsAsErrors>/<NoWarn> elements and never WarningsNotAsErrors, so a multi-line NoWarn, a demoting WarningsNotAsErrors of nullable/CS8618, or an imported value passes.
findings.evidence: probe/src/x.csproj with <NoWarn>\n  CS8602\n</NoWarn> and <WarningsNotAsErrors>nullable;CS8618</WarningsNotAsErrors>: L02 printed nothing. Resolved-property version tested: find src -name '*.csproj' -print0 | xargs -0 -r -n1 dotnet msbuild -nologo -getProperty:NoWarn,WarningsAsErrors,WarningsNotAsErrors | grep -E 'nullable|CS8[0-9]{3}|CS9264' prints the offending lines.
findings.fix: Replace L02 with the per-project msbuild form in the L01a shape (the grep above), keep the file grep as a secondary line for Directory.Build.props, and say empty output passes.

findings.problem: L10c matches AllowUnsafeBlocks set to false, and L10b matches the word 'unsafe' in comments and identifiers; its async-span alternative misses a signature split over two lines (the compiler already errors CS4012/CS4007 on those).
findings.evidence: NLog examples csproj: 2 of 4 L10c hits are <AllowUnsafeBlocks>false</AllowUnsafeBlocks>. L10b over 5 real hits: grpc 'inherently unsafe', NLog 'tread-unsafe!' and 'unsafe to call', RestSharp 'binary search is unsafe' are comments; 1 of 5 (grpc 'public static unsafe string GetString') is a true hit. Probe: 'public static async ValueTask Go(\n Span<byte> x)' not reported; 'string asyncName; void M(Span<int> s)' reported.
findings.fix: L10c pattern 'AllowUnsafeBlocks>[[:space:]]*true'. L10b: split into an unsafe keyword check '\bunsafe[[:space:]]+[A-Za-z{(]' with comment lines dropped via | grep -vE ':[0-9]+:[[:space:]]*(//|\*)' and drop the async-span alternative (CS4012/CS4007 are compile errors under the gate).

findings.problem: L03b matches '!' inside strings and comments, and its 'grep -v null-forgiving:' exempts 'default!' with a trailing reason comment although the rule says default! is never allowed.
findings.evidence: NLog 6 of 14 hits and otel 7 of 154 are prose ('failed! Skipping', '// tread-unsafe!', 'Note! the thing'); restsharp 3 of 75. Probe src/z.cs 'string s = default!; // null-forgiving: reason' produced no L03b output.
findings.fix: Add a second filter for comments/strings, e.g. | grep -vE ':[0-9]+:[[:space:]]*(//|\*|///)' and a separate line 'grep -rnE ... -e \bdefault! src' (no exemption) for the default! ban. Label the remaining hits 'read each: strings and interpolations can still show'.

findings.problem: L05b only matches the unqualified 'new ArgumentNullException(' so 'new System.ArgumentNullException(' and 'new global::System.ArgumentNullException(' pass.
findings.evidence: Probe src/P.cs lines 3-4 (qualified forms) -> L05b printed nothing; red/A.cs used the qualified form, rc=1 with no output.
findings.fix: Pattern 'new[[:space:]]+((global::)?System\.)?ArgumentNullException\('.

findings.problem: L22b '_[[:space:]]*=>[[:space:]]*(true|Ok|Success)' also matches a lambda discard parameter such as .Where(_ => true).
findings.evidence: Probe: 'items.Where(_ => true)' and 'Func<int,bool> f = _ => true;' reported alongside the real switch arm. On real trees the 1 hit (otel PrometheusTranslationStrategyExtensions.cs:72 '_ => true,') is a true fail-open. Anchored variant tested: grep -E '^[[:space:]]*_[[:space:]]*=>[[:space:]]*(true|Ok|Success)\b' reported only the switch arm.
findings.fix: Anchor L22b at line start (switch arms sit on their own line).

findings.problem: L21b is described as a tripwire for casts of collection expressions typed IEnumerable<T> and friends, but matches every cast to List/IList/ICollection/HashSet.
findings.evidence: NLog: 4 of 4 hits are ordinary casts ((ICollection<string>)ArrayHelper.Empty<string>(), (IList<AsyncLogEventInfo>)logEvents), none a collection expression.
findings.fix: Mark L21b 'read each hit; a hit is a violation only when the operand was built by a collection expression or typed IEnumerable<T>/IReadOnly*', or drop it and keep L21a plus the exact-match option.

findings.problem: CS-LANG-25 and L25 treat any partial type without a generator attribute as mimicry, but hand-split partial classes are ordinary C#; the row is SHOULD with a check that is mostly noise, and generators such as [GeneratedComInterface] and [OptionsValidator] are missing from the exemption list.
findings.evidence: RestSharp: L25 lists 24 of 127 src files (RestClient.Extensions.*.cs, RestRequestExtensions.*.cs, PropertyCache.*.cs), all legitimate. NLog adds Logger-generated.cs and ILogger-V1.cs; grpc Shared/ThrowHelpers; kiota KiotaSerializer.*.cs. The consolidation's own failure-mode table never lists 'adds partial' as an agent habit. CS-PERF-03 cites CS-LANG-25.
findings.fix: Delete the row and L25 (retire the ID, update the CS-PERF-03 citation to say 'a partial type that carries the [GeneratedRegex] member'), or reduce to CONSIDER with 'a partial type states why in a comment'.

findings.problem: L11a requires exactly one type token between the accessibility modifier and 'field', so the usual declarations 'private readonly int field;', 'public static int field', 'internal volatile int field' and a bare 'int field;' are missed.
findings.evidence: Probe src/f.cs: only 'protected string? field { get; set; }' reported out of 5 member declarations.
findings.fix: Use -e '[A-Za-z0-9_>?\]][[:space:]]+field[[:space:]]*[;={]' and drop the modifier prefix; keep the note that CS9258 (error under the gate) is the backstop for uses inside accessors.

findings.problem: CS-PERF-04 says to 'take a ReadOnlySpan<T> parameter' for a constant array argument without restricting it to internal helpers, against CS-LANG-10 'No Span<T> or ReadOnlySpan<T> in public signatures' and its L10a check.
findings.evidence: performance.md line 26 vs language.md CS-LANG-10 and L10a (grep Span< in PublicAPI.*.txt).
findings.fix: CS-PERF-04: 'or take a ReadOnlySpan<T> parameter on an internal method (CS-LANG-10 keeps spans off the public surface)'.

findings.problem: The count-style cells (L03a, L05a, L21a, L22a, L24a, L24b) pipe 'grep -c' into 'grep -vx N': when .editorconfig or .globalconfig is absent grep -c writes only to stderr, stdout stays empty, and the cell passes vacuously for anything that discards stderr. L19 names the same files as operands and L19 also never looks at props or csproj.
findings.evidence: p2/: with no .globalconfig, 'grep -cE ... .globalconfig | grep -vx 1' printed nothing on stdout (rc 1). With '2>&1' inside the pipe the missing-file warning surfaces. L19 probe: <NoWarn>$(NoWarn);CS9124</NoWarn> in a csproj produced no L19 hit (cell includes only *.cs, .editorconfig, .globalconfig).
findings.fix: Put '2>&1' on the grep -c before the pipe in the six count cells; add --include='*.props' --include='*.csproj' --include='*.targets' to L19 (as L11c does).

findings.problem: CS-LANG-13 (user-defined compound assignment operators) fails the selection test 'an agent gets it wrong without being told': no corpus frequency, 0 hits in five mature repos, a two-line niche. CS-LANG-02's NoWarn half repeats CS-BUILD-12 and the CS-CORE-01 weaken list; only the WarningsAsErrors-list half is unique.
findings.evidence: L13 had 0 hits in restsharp, otel, NLog, kiota, grpc. CS-BUILD-12 text: 'no analyzer ID in NoWarn' with its own grep over <NoWarn> digits; CS-CORE-01 lists NoWarn beyond NU1900-1905.
findings.fix: Retire CS-LANG-13 (one line in the retired bullet) or fold it into CS-LANG-18/20 as a one-clause SHOULD. Trim CS-LANG-02's Rule to the WarningsAsErrors/WarningsNotAsErrors list and cite CS-BUILD-12 for NoWarn.

findings.problem: CS-LANG-09 states 'every behavioural test runs on every TFM' but L09 only counts distinct TargetFrameworks across projects (also CS-BUILD-01's job). Nothing checks that tests execute per TFM. Separately, several rows (05, 11, 03, 08, 19, 12) carry 1,200-1,700 characters with the measurement log inline, against 'Rationale: one line'.
findings.evidence: Row lengths: CS-LANG-05 1703, -11 1473, -03 1368, -08 1351, -19 1322, -12 1268; mean 926. L09 body: find src tests -name '*.csproj' ... -getProperty:TargetFrameworks | sort -u | wc -l.
findings.fix: Add a run check, e.g. dotnet test -f net8.0 and -f net10.0 both exit 0 (cite CS-TEST-05) or mark that half 'reading heuristic'. Move the per-TFM measurement strings out of the Verification cells of 03, 05, 11 and 12 into the Rationale as one dated clause each.

findings.problem: Corpus statistics appear in rationales without naming or dating the corpus, two external statements are undated, and line 33 cites 'owner default 1' while the index calls it D1 under 'Owner Defaults'.
findings.evidence: Lines 45, 47, 87, 135, 136, 164-166 (221/562, 1,130, 2,155 vs 1,401, 407 vs 12,483, 2,316, 2,028, 8 repos); 'The runtime team's guidance' (row 05) and 'Roslyn calls net8.0 with C# 14 an unsupported configuration' (row 08); csharp-quality.md line 163 '**D1** Reach is net8+ only'.
findings.fix: State once under 'Dates and the Gate': 'Counts are from a corpus audit of public .NET repositories (2026-10-11)' and cite dotnet/runtime nullability guidance and the Roslyn statement with 'read 2026-10-11'. Replace 'owner default 1' with 'D1'.

findings.problem: CS-LANG-10 (spans, stackalloc, unsafe, public overload sets) is reachable only through the performance and security routing rows, neither of which points to language.md; an agent adding a Span parameter or a #if NET11 region reads performance.md or nothing.
findings.evidence: csharp-quality.md line 149 routes Nullable, !, guards, C# 14/15 features, primary constructors, records, collection expressions, switches, #nullable and generated markers to language.md; line 152 routes Span and stackalloc to performance.md; line 150 routes 'an unsafe API' to security.md. performance.md has no CS-LANG-10 pointer.
findings.fix: Extend the line-149 task phrase with 'a Span parameter, unsafe, partial, a preview LangVersion switch or a NET11_0_OR_GREATER region', or add 'see CS-LANG-10' to the CS-PERF-06 row.

reviews.trigger_eval: Glob "**/.csharp-quality-depth-on-demand" matches nothing by design, so the file loads only through the csharp-quality.md routing row at line 149 (Nullable, !, guard clause, C# 14/15 feature, primary constructor, record, collection expression, switch, #nullable, generated-code marker). That covers CS-LANG-01 to 07, 11 to 12, 15, 18 to 24 well. Gaps: CS-LANG-10 (Span, stackalloc, unsafe) routes to performance.md and security.md only, and CS-LANG-16 (#if NET11_0_OR_GREATER), CS-LANG-25 (partial) and the LangVersion/preview switch (CS-LANG-15) have no task phrase; CS-LANG-15 is partly reachable via dotnet-build.md CS-BUILD-04, CS-LANG-16 via dotnet-upgrade. See F17.

reviews.report:
PHASE 8 REVIEW: ADR + docs pages + bundle (unit: adr_ocx_csharp_sdk.md, docs/csharp-quality, dotnet-build, dotnet-upgrade, dotnet-diagnose, dotnet-release, dotnet-essentials, bundles/dotnet-essentials.toml). Worktree untouched. Fixtures under .../fixtures/review-adr-docs/ (red/, green/, cells/ extracted verbatim from the ADR, real/ = golden JSON fetched from ocx-sh/ocx@3485207c1, m8/ m11/ v1/ v5*/ mutation sets).

ORCHESTRATOR DIRECTIVE (ocx-sh/ocx#604): gh says MERGED, mergedAt 2026-10-10T22:49:47Z, merge commit 3485207c183e. The ADR already says "merged 2026-10-10 as 3485207c1" (Decision Drivers) and uses past tense in Risks. No ADR edit is needed. The only stale text is the last bullet of "Open for the owner" in csharp-topic-map.md's Integration log ("The ADR still calls #604 open"): strike it (F10). Other upstream facts re-read with gh/curl/jq and confirmed: v0.6.5 is the latest tag and is 1 commit behind 6daf9a164; main is 15 ahead of v0.6.5 and equals 3485207c1; no tag contains 6daf9a164; dist.json = 280 rows / 35 versions / 8 targets / 88,245 B; release assets carry a `digest` field and sha256.sum; archives are about 11 MB; golden at 3485207c1: 13 exit codes, 11 categories, 516 detail slugs, cli.json 81 nodes, 124 env (56 public, 66 foreign, 2 plumbing), 13 root args, output modes 65/17/10/7/5/1, reports 56, 7 passthrough nodes, 4 error-on-invalid env vars. ocx-sh/www-setup#14 is open.

1. VERIFICATION HONESTY. The ADR holds the unit's only runnable cells, V1 to V11 (docs and bundle carry no checks, only `grim add` lines). Each was run verbatim through bash against a planted RED and a GREEN twin, plus targeted mutations; the rg cells (V1,V3,V4,V5,V6,V7,V9) ran over 5 held-out trees (RestSharp, OpenTelemetry, grpc-dotnet, kiota, NLog).
 - V1 FAIL: red 1 hit (ok), but the GREEN twin also prints (`exitCode == 0`). 0 and 1 are table rows, so the comment "a hit is an exit literal outside the table" is false for `== 0`/`!= 0`/`== 1` sites every engine has. Also misses `r.Code`, `exitcode`. It is a different regex from the shipped owner CS-ERR-02 check 02a (`\b(?:[eE]xit)?[cC]ode(\.Value)?\s*(==|!=|is)\s*[1-9]\d{0,2}\b`), which the integration log says "owns the pattern". Both miss `75 == code`, `rc == 75`, `switch`/`case 75`/`code switch { 75 => }` (known limits, fine to state). F1.
 - V9 FAIL on real trees: `\bevent\s+` matches prose. NLog 152 hits, OpenTelemetry 28, kiota 3 (grpc 3 are real IAsyncEnumerable). I read 20 sampled hits: 20 of 20 were comments, XML doc or attribute text ("log event", "event payload"), 0 declarations. A replacement that anchors on a declaration (`^\s*(?!//)[^"/]*\bevent\s+[\w<>?.,\s]+\s\w+\s*[;{]`) gives NLog 12 true event declarations, OTel 0, kiota 0, red fixture 3/3, green 0. F2.
 - V2 ok: red (82 removed or 83 appended) exits 1, green exits 0, and it prints true on the real golden errors.json at 3485207c1.
 - V3 ok on fixture (red hit, green exit 1 empty). Note it flags any mention of the names in src, including a doc comment explaining why they are not set; acceptable.
 - V4 ok (red 2, green 1). V6 red 3 / green 1, but the pattern is a prefix: `TestedOcxVersion2` counts. V7 ok (red 1, green 2).
 - V5 ok for the shape CS-PROC-21 mandates (sealed class): red prints the file, green is empty with xargs 123. It is silent if ChildExit becomes a record or struct; CS-PROC-21 forbids that, so not a finding, but the cell should say so.
 - V8 weak: red cases (7 pins, upper-case, short, 9 pins, no version) all exit 1, but a pin with a trailing newline and a `pins` array both PASS (`$` matches before a final newline; no object check). Fix tested: `(.pins|type=="object")` and `test("\\A[0-9a-f]{64}\\z")` rejects both and still passes green. F13.
 - V10 ok (red exit 1, green 0). V11: dup id, short table, wrong unknown-code row, schema 2 all exit 1; missing unknown-code row exits 4 (jq -e no output); green exit 0. ok.
 - No placeholders in any cell. The ADR's own header "watched red and green" is true for V2, V3, V4, V6, V7, V8 (basic), V9, V10, V11, V5; false for V1 as shipped.
 Beyond the cells I re-ran three claims the docs rest on: the dotnet-upgrade R3 probe (six IDs CA1517, CA1876, CA1877, CA2026, CA2027, CA2028 printed, matches docs), malformed global.json selects 11.0.100-rc.1 (true on this host), and the MSB4242 cascade (F11).

2. FIDELITY. No rule rows live in this unit. The ADR cites 100+ IDs; every cited ID exists as a row in the shipped files, and the seven retired IDs (CS-ASYNC-24, CS-ASYNC-28, CS-BIN-19, CS-BIN-23, CS-BIN-27, CS-BIN-28, CS-OBS-25) are marked "retired, not reused" in their owning files and decided in D5/D7/D8/D9 as N-7 requires. Ranges (CS-BIN-04..09, 20..22, 24..26, CS-ERR-12..17, CS-TEST-27..31) all resolve. Numbers in D1 to D13 trace to csharp-process/packaging/async/audit and to the golden files. Deviations: ADR says "six retired rows" in Context but lists seven (F4); D2 row 69 gloss differs from the upstream doc comment (F9); D6 secret and scrub lists (F5, F6).

reviews.report:
PHASE 8 REVIEW, UNIT security.md + observability.md (rules/csharp-quality/), worktree csharp, 2026-10-11. Read-only on the worktree. Fixtures: /home/mherwig/.cache/research-lang/dotnet-tools/fixtures/review-security-obs/ (sg, sup, gate, ban, pack, nus, lic, reg, dep, sig, bc, og, ob). SDK 10.0.401 pinned by global.json, nets net8.0/net9.0/net10.0, BannedApiAnalyzers 5.6.0.

VERDICT: not ready. 15 of ~58 cells fail honesty (cannot go red where they must, go red on green or real compliant trees, or are not runnable verbatim). Ten findings are majors. The two highest-impact structural problems: (1) a real rule contradiction on suppressing RS0030, (2) three of the greps that police the *mandated* style (generated [LoggerMessage] methods) cannot see that style at all.

1. VERIFICATION HONESTY
Cells run (verbatim from the unit, red + green twin unless noted):
- security gate block (4): SEC-01 msbuild/jq loop red on AnalysisLevel=10.0-recommended (printed tests/T/T.csproj), green with AnalysisModeSecurity=All: OK. SEC-02 uniq -d and grep -c 2: ran green OK, but FALSE POSITIVE with the documented install copy (F3). SEC-02 `dotnet build -p:TreatWarningsAsErrors=false`: not runnable as written (F4); with canary path + Variant=Bad: exit 1, 12 RS0030 errors (3 sites x 2 TFM x log dup); without the .globalconfig lines: exit 0 with warnings. Confirms the rationale.
- security greps block (10): 03a, 03b, 04, 05, 06a, 06b, 07, 16, 08a, 08b. Red/green ran. 03a, 03b, 05, 06a, 06b, 08b have defects (F2, F6, F7, F11, F12).
- security pack block (5): 09a/09b red (2 and 4 deps with bare MinVer+BannedApiAnalyzers) green 0/0: OK. 10a printed MinVer + analyzer pack red, nothing green: OK. 10b matched a planted single-line PackageVersion PrivateAssets, misses a wrapped element (minor, folded into F9 note). 16a printed 1 red (planted _manifest), 0 green: OK.
- build code block (6): imports check red/green OK (empty list prints minver, bannedapianalyzers, system.text.json; listing silences). Analyzers check red/green OK. Triage cells run on the real MinVer nupkg and a planted evil.helper nupkg: work, but cand.nupkg origin unspecified (F25). SEC-12 curl cell ran network: NOT-FOUND works; green not empty (F8). SEC-13 eng/licenses.sh executed verbatim: green closure prints nothing, planted NO-SPDX and GPL lines print, exceptions file silences the exact line (format unstated, F25).
- registry block (5): awk, grep -c, default-days 0, DOTNET_NUGET_SIGNATURE_VERIFICATION grep, xmllint: red/green OK for the documented cases; gaps in F9, F10.
- observability greps (21 rg lines) on a planted red tree and green twin, plus a second red tree for forms the first did not plant; nuspec greps (a)(b)(c) red (Abstractions 10.0.0 + MEL impl) and green (8.0.0) and a DiagnosticSource package: OK, all three go red and green correctly. Build checks: red project (ext call, $"" template, dup EventId, unreferenced param, Console/Debug/Trace/Progress<T>, AddException on net8) fails with CA2254, CA1848, CA1873, SYSLIB1006, SYSLIB1015, RS0030 x16, CS1061; green twin exits 0; without the 16 lines at 10.0-all CA2254/CA1848/CA1873 fail and SYSLIB1006 does not: matches the unit text.
- Held-out: all rg cells over open-telemetry__opentelemetry-dotnet, grpc__grpc-dotnet, restsharp__RestSharp, NLog__NLog, microsoft__kiota-dotnet; hits sampled and read (SEC-03a 21 hits, 100% FP; OBS-06 13 hits, 100% FP; OBS-20 kiota 11/13 FP; etc.).

2. FIDELITY
IDs stable (SEC-01..16, OBS-01..24, 26..29), CS-OBS-25 marked retired in the intro, severities match the consolidations (SEC-07/08/13/14/15 SHOULD, SEC-16 CONSIDER, OBS-05/08 SHOULD, OBS-11 CONSIDER). Authorised divergences present (S1 regex, SEC-01 CA5350/CA5359 exceptions, SEC-06 vs CS-BUILD-12 stricter, OBS-02 test relaxation via CS-TEST-12, OBS-13 owner exception). Unfaithful items: SEC-08 dropped SequenceEqual from the grep but still says hits are reviewed (F7); OBS-03 rewording is fine; the Src ban file has a sixth line (CS-OBS-27 Progress`1) that the unit omits (F22); the Defaults bullet cites "the five span tags" which exist only in the retired OBS-25 (F21).

3. CONTRADICTION
F1 SEC-06 vs CS-ASYNC-14 and both ban-file headers (RS0030 pragma). F24 SEC-08 SHOULD vs CS-BIN-07/CS-BIN-20 MUST that route through its helper. F2 SEC-03a vs CS-PROC-16 (every compliant library mentions InfiniteTimeSpan). No other contradictions found: SEC-07 agrees with CS-BIN-18/CS-PROC-22, OBS-26 with CS-PROC-07, OBS-28 with CS-ERR-06/CS-ASYNC-30, OBS-13 with SEC-09.

4. DELETION TEST
H12 (static Pbkdf2/RSA 1024; "the library derives no keys"), H14 and H16 duplicate SEC-07 / SEC-03 and carry no check; CS-OBS-23's AddException clause duplicates OBS-20/21 and the compiler (CS1061) self-corrects (F23). Nothing else is pure restatement; OBS-01/02 are not redundant with the analyzers because the SDK default hides them.

No /home/ paths. ocx instance names are labelled examples in the OBS header; acceptable. 6. READING

"Eight hazard classes" vs a 9-row table that omits TLS and ECDsa (F23). Rows are multi-sentence paragraphs against the "one imperative sentence" anatomy, uniform across the corpus, not itemised.

findings.evidence: ban/ canary at 10.0-all with shipped BannedSymbols.txt and .globalconfig: only `Assembly.LoadFrom` (line 7) raised RS0030; lines using Assembly.Load(string), Load(byte[]), a.GetType(p), Activator.CreateInstanceFrom, AppDomain.CreateInstance, LoadFromAssemblyPath built without any diagnostic.
findings.fix: Add to the CS-SEC section of BannedSymbols.txt: M:System.Reflection.Assembly.Load(System.String), Load(System.Byte[]), Load(System.Reflection.AssemblyName), M:System.Reflection.Assembly.GetType(System.String) (+ the 2 other overloads), M:System.Activator.CreateInstanceFrom(System.String,System.String), M:System.Runtime.Loader.AssemblyLoadContext.LoadFromAssemblyPath(System.String); update the '7 lines' counts in SEC-04, H5 and the Decisions text. Also add `rg -n -e 'Assembly\.Load' -e 'CreateInstanceFrom' src` to the SEC-04 grep as a backstop.

findings.problem: The '18 ban lines' do not close every Regex form without a timeout: `[GeneratedRegex(p, opts, "en-US")]` (3-arg culture overload), static `Regex.Replace(s,p,MatchEvaluator[,opts])` and static `Regex.Count(...)` (string and span) all build clean. CS-PERF-03's G2 grep catches the static calls but not the GeneratedRegex culture overload, so SEC-03 (a csharp-quality non-negotiable) has a hole.
findings.evidence: ban/ canary: lines using GeneratedRegex("a", RegexOptions.None, "en-US"), Regex.Replace(s,p,m=>"x"), Regex.Replace(...,RegexOptions.None), Regex.Count(s,p), Regex.Count(span,p) produced no RS0030; the ctor, IsMatch, Match/Matches/Split and EnumerateMatches(ROS) lines did. G2 in performance.md:40 lists Count and Replace but not GeneratedRegex.
findings.fix: Add bans for GeneratedRegexAttribute.#ctor(String,RegexOptions,String), Regex.Count (4 overloads), Regex.Replace(String,String,MatchEvaluator) and (..,RegexOptions); then correct '18 ban lines' in SEC-03, H15 and Decisions. Cheaper backstop: add `\[GeneratedRegex\([^)]*\)\]` without `matchTimeoutMilliseconds` to the SEC-03 greps.

findings.problem: Both SEC-06 greps are bypassable by the exact moves the rule fears: (a) `[SuppressMessage("Design"|"Microsoft.Security", "CA5351")]` suppresses the diagnostic (category is ignored) but the grep only matches category "Security"; (b) `dotnet_diagnostic.CA5351.severity = None` (capital N) suppresses, grep is case-sensitive; (c) `<WarningsNotAsErrors>CA5351</WarningsNotAsErrors>` downgrades to warning, not scanned; (d) the config grep globs `.globalconfig` only, so a lowering in `extra.globalconfig` or `eng/x.globalconfig` is invisible (CS-BUILD-11 globs both).
findings.evidence: sup/ project at 10.0-all + TWAE: baseline error CA5351; with SuppressMessage("Design"...) 0 errors; with SuppressMessage("Microsoft.Security"...) 0 errors; with `severity = None` 0 errors; with WarningsNotAsErrors 0 errors / 1 warning. sg/r3: `extra.globalconfig` with `CA5351.severity = none` -> verbatim cell exit 1 (no hit); with `--glob '*.globalconfig'` it hits.
findings.fix: Change cell 1 to match by ID: `SuppressMessage\([^)]*"($SEC)\b` (drop the "Security" literal); run the config grep with `rg -i` and add `--glob '*.globalconfig'` and `-e "WarningsNotAsErrors[^<]*($SEC)"`.

findings.problem: The consolidation's grep was `SequenceEqual\(|MD5\.|SHA1\.` printing nothing. The unit dropped SequenceEqual from the pattern yet its comment and the rule still say 'SequenceEqual hits outside the helper are reviewed'. No command finds a hand-written compare, which is the whole defect the 'one helper' rule exists to prevent (three drifting compares).
findings.evidence: sg/h8: a src/C.cs with `a.SequenceEqual(b)` plus a single FixedTimeEquals helper: count cell prints 1, `rg -n -e 'MD5\.' -e 'SHA1\.' src` prints nothing, so the hand-rolled compare passes both cells. Consolidation csharp-security.md CS-SEC-08 Verify line 2.
findings.fix: Add a review-aid line: `rg -n 'SequenceEqual\(' src   # CS-SEC-08 review aid: each hit outside the helper compares non-authentication bytes`, and keep the MD5/SHA1 line as the 'prints nothing' cell.

findings.problem: The row claims the build-code block cell 'prints nothing' and the watched text says 'the two analyzer packs printed nothing', but on the shipped Directory.Packages.analyzers.props the cell prints two UNVERIFIED lines, so it cannot be green on the unit's own posture. It also misses PackageVersion elements whose Include is not the first attribute or is on a new line, and hard-codes azuresearch-usnc.nuget.org instead of resolving the SearchQueryService from the service index.
findings.evidence: reg/: shipped posture props -> `UNVERIFIED IDisposableAnalyzers owners=JohanLarsson`, `UNVERIFIED MinVer owners=adamralph`. A props file with `<PackageVersion Version="1.0" Include="Foo.Bar.Baz.Nonexist"/>` and a wrapped `<PackageVersion\n Include="Newtonsoft.Jsonn"/>` printed nothing for either (only the well-ordered unknown ID printed NOT-FOUND).
findings.fix: Redefine the pass: no `NOT-FOUND`, and every `UNVERIFIED` ID appears in a checked-in `eng/package-owners.txt` (`grep -v -x -f` it) so the posture packs are listed once with owner. Match IDs with `-o 'Include="[^"]+"'` after `rg -U '<(PackageVersion|GlobalPackageReference)[^>]*>'`. Resolve the query host from https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json (type SearchQueryService).

findings.problem: The dependabot cells enforce 'never 0' but the rule says cooldown of at least 3. `default-days: 1` and `2` pass. The awk also passes on a commented `# cooldown:` line and fails when `cooldown:` precedes `package-ecosystem:` in the entry (valid YAML key order). The `PackageVersion` grep of CS-SEC-10 misses a wrapped element (multi-line attributes).
findings.evidence: dep/red3 (default-days: 1): awk exit 0, grep for 0 exit 1 (passes). dep/edge: commented `# cooldown:` -> awk exit 0 (false pass); cooldown listed before package-ecosystem -> awk exit 1 (false fail). pack/pv: wrapped `<PackageVersion Include=.. \n PrivateAssets="all"/>` -> grep exit 1.
findings.fix: Use `grep -nE 'default-days: *[0-2]\b' .github/dependabot.yml` (prints nothing); strip comments before awk (`sed 's/#.*//'`) and track the entry with `/^  - /`; use `rg -U` for the PackageVersion check.

findings.problem: The signature-verification grep is case-sensitive (`False`, `FALSE`) and limited to yml/yaml/props/sh, so `ENV DOTNET_NUGET_SIGNATURE_VERIFICATION=false` in a Dockerfile, .targets, .ps1 or .cmd passes.
findings.evidence: sig/red: Dockerfile `ENV ...=false` and a workflow `'False'` produced no hit; only ci.yml and x.sh hit.
findings.fix: Use `rg -i -n 'DOTNET_NUGET_SIGNATURE_VERIFICATION[=:"'"'"' ]+false' .` (drops the --include list; ripgrep honours .gitignore).

findings.problem: `using System\.Xml` bans the namespace, but `System.Xml` is imported only for `XmlConvert` (ISO-8601 TimeSpan/duration, bool) in JSON libraries; that is not XML parsing. Reviewers learn to ignore the cell.
findings.evidence: Held-out kiota-dotnet (JSON/Form/Text serializers): 7/7 SEC-05 hits are `using System.Xml;` for XmlConvert. grpc and NLog hits are DllImport in a non-JSON-wire tree (out of scope), pragma/comment text.
findings.fix: Match parser types instead of the namespace: `-e 'XmlReader|XmlDocument|XDocument|XmlSerializer|XmlTextReader|XslCompiledTransform|XPathDocument'`, and keep `System.Data`, DllImport, LibraryImport, BinaryFormatter, Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration as is.

findings.problem: The CS-SEC-03 review aid `Regex\.(IsMatch|...)\(...` has no left boundary, so instance calls on a variable named `fooRegex.Replace(x, ...)` match; and it misses the target-typed `Regex X = new(pattern)` that CS-PERF-03 forbids.
findings.evidence: kiota-dotnet: 3/3 hits are `queryParametersCleanupRegex.Replace(...)` / `contentTypeVendorCleanupRegex.Replace(...)` instance calls. sg/red: `static readonly Regex R3 = new(pattern);` not listed while `new Regex(pattern)` is.
findings.fix: Add `(?<![\w.])Regex\.` before the static-method group and a third alternative `\bRegex\s+\w+\s*=\s*new\s*\((?!@?")`.

findings.problem: The Serilog-operator grep only looks at `LogX("...{@X}")` extension calls with the string as the first argument, but CS-OBS-02 requires every template to live in a `[LoggerMessage]` attribute (`Message = "...{@X}"` or the positional string). The operators therefore pass undetected in all compliant code, and in extension calls whose first argument is an exception or EventId.
findings.evidence: og/r2: `[LoggerMessage(EventId=1, ..., Message = "x {@Pkg} {$Y}")]` and `[LoggerMessage(2, LogLevel.Information, "x {@Pkg}")]` -> no hit; `_l.LogInformation("x {@Pkg}", 1)` hits (line 27).
findings.fix: Add `-e 'Message\s*=\s*"[^"]*\{[@$]\w+' -e '\[LoggerMessage\([^)]*"[^"]*\{[@$]\w+'` and loosen the first pattern to `Log\w*\([^;"]*"[^"]*\{[@$]\w+`.

findings.problem: The pattern `Log\w*\([^;]*\b\w*[eE]x\w*\.(Message|ToString())` has no left boundary and requires the variable name to contain 'ex'. It fires on `NLogConfigurationException($"..{ex.Message}", ex)` and `AddLogAttribute(.., logRecord.Exception.Message)`, and misses `catch (Exception e)` + `e.Message` and every generated method not named Log* (e.g. `_l.Failed(ex.Message)`), i.e. the style CS-OBS-02 mandates. Result: 0 true positives, all hits false.
findings.evidence: Held-out NLog 12/12 hits = `new NLogConfigurationException($"...{ex.Message}", ex)`; OTel 1/1 = AddLogAttribute(..Exception.Message). og/r2: `_l.Failed(ex.Message)`, `_l.LogError("x {M}", e.Message)` (var `e`) and `_l.Failed(ex2.ToString())` -> no hit.
findings.fix: Anchor at a logger receiver and take any arg: `(?i:\blog\w*)\??\.\w+\([^;]*\b(\w+)\.(Message|ToString\(\))` restricted to variables bound by `catch (... (\w+))` is not expressible in one rg; ship `rg -n -U -P 'catch\s*\([^)]*\b(\w+)\)[^{]*\{[^{}]*\w+\([^;]*\b\1\.(Message|ToString\(\))'` as the review aid, and keep the `{Ex}` pattern with `(?<![\w])Log`.

findings.problem: The log-and-rethrow grep requires `.Log\w+(` inside the catch. CS-OBS-02 makes generated methods the only log calls, usually named for the event (`_l.ConnectionFailed(ex)`), so the grep sees only the forbidden extension style and misses the defect in compliant code.
findings.evidence: og/r2: `catch (Exception x) { _l.Failed("a"); throw; }` and a multi-line `catch (Exception ex2) { _l.Failed(ex2.ToString()); throw; }` -> verbatim cell prints nothing; the red tree's `_l.LogError(e, "x"); throw;` hits.
findings.fix: Match any call that passes the catch variable before a `throw;`: `catch\s*\([^)]*\b(\w+)\)[^{]*\{[^{}]*\w+\.\w+\([^;]*\b\1\b[^;]*;[^{}]*\bthrow\s*;`, and keep the single-block caveat.

findings.problem: `\[LoggerMessage\((?![^\]]*EventId)` flags the valid positional form `[LoggerMessage(2, LogLevel.Information, "x")]` (explicit id) and any attribute whose Message contains `]` before EventId; it also hits a comment mentioning `[LoggerMessage]`.
findings.evidence: og/r2 line 4 positional and line 7 (`Message = "list [a] {M}", EventId = 5`) flagged; OTel LogRecord.cs:523 comment hit.
findings.fix: Either forbid positional in the rule text ('EventId as a named property') or tighten: `(?![^\n]*(EventId|\(\s*\d+\s*,))`; skip `//` lines with `-g '*.cs' --glob` plus `^(?!\s*//)`.

findings.problem: `StartActivity\(\$` flags `$"{nameof(A)}_{nameof(B)}"`, which is a compile-time constant, not an interpolated closed table; the allow-list diff reads only `SetTag("literal"` so metric tag keys (`KeyValuePair<string,object?>("k", v)`, `TagList`), `AddTag`, and `SetTag(Keys.X, ..)` pass unseen though the rule covers span AND metric attributes with literal keys.
findings.evidence: kiota-dotnet 11 of 13 OBS-20 hits are nameof-only names. og/r2: `Duration.Record(1, new KeyValuePair<string, object?>("package","x"))` and `activity.SetTag(Keys.Pkg,"x")` yield an empty diff.
findings.fix: Exempt nameof-only interpolations (`StartActivity\(\$"(?!\{nameof\([^)]*\)\}(_\{nameof\([^)]*\)\})*")`) and add `rg -n 'SetTag\((?!")' -P src` plus a metric-tag key scan (`KeyValuePair<string, ?object\?>\("([^"]+)"` into the same diff).

findings.problem: CS-OBS-22 and CS-OBS-24 count matching LINES (`rg -c`), not instruments or listeners. Two instruments on one line count as one (cell passes); a `new ActivityListener` and a `Sample =` for a different object on separate lines can offset.
findings.evidence: og/red: a line with `m.CreateHistogram<double>(..); m.CreateCounter<int>(..);` -> exit 0 (should be 1). Two `new ActivityListener {..}` on one line plus no Sample -> L=1,S=0 exit 1 only by luck.
findings.fix: Use `rg -o` and count: `rg -o -g '*.cs' -e 'Create(Histogram|Counter|UpDownCounter|Gauge|Observable\w*)\b' src | wc -l` must print 1; same for the listener pair.

findings.problem: Several greps match shared prefixes and unrelated receivers: `Mock<ILogger` also matches `Mock<ILoggerFactory>`/`ILoggerProvider`; CS-OBS-02's `.LogError(`/`.LogWarning(` match any CLI helper (`console.LogError(e)`); CS-OBS-29's `-i baggage` matches every `Activity.Baggage`/`context.Baggage` use.
findings.evidence: grpc-dotnet OBS-12 2/2 = Mock<ILoggerFactory>; OBS-02 9 of 11 = dotnet-grpc `console.LogError`; OTel OBS-29 266 baggage hits of 494. NLog OBS-02 2 hits = Debugger.Log / ILoggerBase.Log.
findings.fix: OBS-12: `Mock<ILogger(<|>)`. OBS-29: restrict to env use: `-e '"TRACEPARENT"' -e '"TRACESTATE"' -e '"BAGGAGE"' -e 'Environment\[[^]]*(traceparent|tracestate|baggage)'` with -i. OBS-02: leave, but say hits on a non-ILogger receiver are not findings.

findings.problem: The intro says BinaryFormatter 'the type is removed on net9 and later'. The type still exists on net9 and net10 and fails to compile with error SYSLIB0011; the implementation was removed, the type remains as an always-throwing stub.
findings.evidence: sup/ with net8.0;net9.0;net10.0: `new System.Runtime.Serialization.Formatters.Binary.BinaryFormatter()` -> `error SYSLIB0011: 'BinaryFormatter' is obsolete` on all three TFMs, no CS0246.
findings.fix: Reword: 'SYSLIB0011 is a compile error from net7, the runtime throws on net8, and net9 and later keep an always-throwing stub'.

findings.problem: Two stale references: the Defaults bullet cites 'the five span tags' that exist only in the retired CS-OBS-25 (the unit never lists them, so the reader cannot act); and the Posture bullet says BannedSymbols.Src.txt carries the CS-OBS-16 lines, while the file also carries a sixth ban `T:System.Progress`1;CS-OBS-27` that CS-OBS-27's verification never mentions.
findings.evidence: observability.md:31-32 vs :19-20 (OBS-25 retired); BannedSymbols.Src.txt line 64 `System.Progress`1;CS-OBS-27: callbacks are inline Action<string>; Progress<T> po...`; ob/ build raised RS0030 for `new Progress<string>` (16 RS0030 on the red project).
findings.fix: Replace 'the five span tags' with 'the span tag set' (pointing at CS-OBS-20's allow-list); add 'RS0030 from the CS-OBS-27 line of BannedSymbols.Src.txt' to the CS-OBS-27 Verification and 'and the CS-OBS-27 `Progress<T>` line' to the Posture bullet.

findings.problem: Deletion-test and reading issues: H12 (static Pbkdf2/RSA 1024, 'the library derives no keys'), H14 and H16 restate CS-SEC-07/CS-SEC-03 with no check of their own; CS-OBS-23 duplicates CS-OBS-20/21's AddException ban and its other APIs fail with a compiler error the agent self-corrects; the Decisions bullet says 'Eight hazard classes' but the table has 9 rows and omits the TLS-hook and ECDsa classes the same bullet counts; the registry block header says 'empty output passes' though the grep -c cell prints a count.
findings.evidence: security.md:54-67 table vs :39; :128 header vs :130 `grep -c ... # at least 1`; observability.md:126 CS-OBS-23 vs :123 CS-OBS-20.
findings.fix: Delete H12, H14, H16; add TLS and ECDsa rows (or say 'seven ban classes'); trim CS-OBS-23 to InstrumentAdvice and the 3-arg ActivitySource ctor; change the registry header to 'exit codes and counts as stated per line'.

findings.problem: CS-SEC-08 is SHOULD, but CS-BIN-07 (MUST) and CS-BIN-20 (MUST) hard-require the same helper ('as bytes through the CS-SEC-08 helper'). A MUST routes through a rule whose severity lets the reviewer accept a justification.
findings.evidence: binaries.md CS-BIN-07 and CS-BIN-20 rows (MUST) vs security.md CS-SEC-08 row (SHOULD); consolidation kept SEC-08 SHOULD.
findings.fix: Raise CS-SEC-08 to MUST for the archive/pin/sidecar callers (keep SHOULD only for 'any other compare'), or word CS-BIN-07/20 as 'through one helper' without citing a SHOULD row.

findings.problem: Several cells lack a step or prerequisite: `cand.nupkg` is 'the candidate package' but nothing says it comes from the packages folder after a restore (restore runs no package code; build does); `unzip -p cand.nupkg '*.targets' '*.props'` prints 'caution: filename not matched' (exit 11) when a package has no .props; the line format of `eng/license-exceptions.txt` is not stated (it must be the exact `<id>/<version> <SPDX>` line the script prints for `grep -v -x -f` to silence it) and compound SPDX such as `MIT OR Apache-2.0` is reported; jq, xmllint, unzip, curl are used but no prerequisite line lists them.
findings.evidence: bc/: real MinVer nupkg and a planted evil.helper nupkg from the packages folder -> stderr caution on missing *.props; lic/: `dual 1.0.0 (MIT AND GPL-3.0-only)` printed, exceptions file silenced only after writing `evil.helper/1.0.0 NO-SPDX-EXPRESSION` verbatim.
findings.fix: Add one line to Dates and Defaults: 'tools: rg, jq, xmllint, unzip, curl'; add 'restore first; the file is <packages>/<id>/<ver>/<id>.<ver>.nupkg' to SEC-11; add 2>/dev/null to the unzip triage; state the exceptions-line format and that compound expressions are a human decision in SEC-13.

reviews.report:
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, phase 8, unit rules/csharp-quality/platform-and-paths.md + performance.md (worktree csharp, read-only; nothing written there). Fixtures: /home/mherwig/.cache/research-lang/dotnet-tools/fixtures/review-platform-perf/ (xp-red/green, perf-red/green, xpb-red/green and perf2/perfb build fixtures with the SHIPPED posture files from rules/dotnet-build/checks, g1-*, g11-*, bdn, ps, rt, fixes.sh). Toolchain SDK 10.0.401 via run.sh, net8.0 and net10.0. Plain `rg` in this harness is rewritten, so every run used the absolute ripgrep 15.2.0 with PCRE2.

VERDICT: no blockers. 5 majors, 14 minors. Row IDs, severities and retired-ID notes are faithful to the consolidations and the authoring notes; every cited ID resolves; every internal anchor resolves; no /home paths or research-host names leak; ocx names are labelled examples; files over 100 lines carry a Contents line. The weak spots are verification cells, not rule text.

1. VERIFICATION HONESTY (35 cells run, 3 failed)
Passed on planted red and green twin: dotnet build gate (red: RS0030 on all 12 XP ban groups incl. the 5-arg span Path.Combine, CA1304/1305/1307/1309/1310/1311, CA1416, MA0076, per TFM; green exit 0; tests project stays clean for DateTime/Thread.Sleep and red for SetCurrentDirectory/Path.Combine, as claimed); P1; P2; ReparsePoint; InvariantGlobalization; tr-TR; -windows TFM; Split; G1 (also green on the shipped analyzers.globalconfig + analyzers.editorconfig); G2 to G5, G7, G10, G11; params/catch/Bdn/test ! -d lists; PathSafe reference shape against the 12-row table plus 16 adversarial inputs (all correct on Linux); build claims for SYSLIB1045 (only fires with the line; also fires alone on static Regex.Count, so the line is not redundant with the RS0030 bans), CA1867/CA1865, CA1822 option (internal flagged, public not), CA1861 vs collection expression, CA1862 blind to Equals(..., Ordinal) and collection Contains, CA2014; runtime claims (Registry NRE on Linux, de-DE gives 1,5 and parse 15, invariant mode throws on new CultureInfo, Personal=~/Documents when it exists, GetFolderPath empty for a missing HOME, GetInvalidFileNameChars=2, the ReadOnlySpan ban line load-bearing on net10.0 only).
FAILED:
 a. CS-PERF-02 count cell prints nothing (exit 1) on the shipped analyzers.globalconfig: the patterns end in `$` but the row requires, and the shipped file carries, a trailing `# CS-PERF-02`. It prints 3 only on a hand-stripped file. Fixed pattern (`( #.*)?$`) prints 3 on the shipped file.
 b. Procedure step 4 assertion stays green on a stale report: after one real run, a second run with a filter matching zero benchmarks exits 0, prints "returned 0 benchmarks" and the test -n assertion still passes (the results directory persists). After `rm -rf BenchmarkDotNet.Artifacts` first, it goes red.
 c. G6 goes red on the rule's own green forms: `stackalloc byte[MaxStack]` and `stackalloc byte[16 * 1024]` print. On open-telemetry-dotnet and grpc-dotnet, 13 of 19 hits are named constants (TraceIdSizeInBytes, Limit, MaxFreeSlotCandidates, StackallocByteThreshold, MaxFormattedDoubleCharacters x4, HeaderSize, a product of two consts), plus 1 guarded by `if (value.Length <= Threshold) {` on the previous line. Fixed pattern (digits or PascalCase identifiers and + - * of them count as constant) removes the planted FPs and cuts otel from 17 to 6.
Partial misses and FPs found by planted probes and held-out trees are findings below (G2, G3, G4, G5, G8, G9, G10, G11, P2, XP-06, XP-08, XP-09, XP-12).
Held-out trees used: open-telemetry-dotnet, grpc-dotnet, NLog, RestSharp, kiota-dotnet, Newtonsoft.Json, MailKit (src operand replaced by `.`, so test dirs are included; I discounted test hits). G5 on real code: 4 hit files (grpc Base64RequestStream field buffer returned in Dispose; grpc StreamExtensions grow-swap Rent/Return then final Return in finally; otel PooledList struct; Newtonsoft adapter wrapper), 0 genuine violations. G8 strict finds 1 non-test hit in 16 trees (Bogus) and misses Bicep ExpressionHelpers.cs:32 (the loop body has an `if { current += ... }`); a looser pattern finds both. G3 on src: 1 otel hit (a static readonly, passes) and grpc one-shot Option ctor args (not loops); signal is low.

2. FIDELITY
All 12 XP and 9 PERF rows match consolidation meaning and severity (XP-12 and PERF-04,05,07,08,09 SHOULD; rest MUST). IDs stable; CS-BIN-03 and CS-BUILD-07 marked retired as N-7 requires (CS-BUILD-07 also in dotnet-build.md). Deliberate deviations all trace to notes/integration log (CA1849/CA1848/CA1873 exclusions in G1, P1 ordering, TimeProvider supersession of CS-PROC-15/22). Real fidelity gaps: PERF-03 turns the validator-only `\A..\z` anchor of CS-BIN-08 into a rule for every literal regex (F13); PERF-02 keeps the consolidation's optional MA0110 line even though Meziantou is in the posture and MA0110 adds nothing (F10); XP-04 omits the rooted requirement that CS-BIN-13 attributes to it (F5).

3. CONTRADICTION
 - CS-XP-04 accepts any non-empty variable; CS-BIN-13 says a relative variable counts as unset and calls that "the CS-XP-04 cwd hazard". A relative HOME yields the cwd-relative root XP-04 exists to prevent.
 - The XP gate line `dotnet build --no-incremental` and PERF step 4 `dotnet run -c Release ...` do not follow DN-RULE-01 (timeout, redirect to a file), DN-RULE-02 / CS-BUILD-30 (`--tl:off --interactive false`) and DN-RULE-10 (`--disable-build-servers`); async.md and binaries.md write the compliant form.
 No other same-subject conflicts: TimeProvider forms agree with CS-PROC-15/22, CS-ASYNC-08, CS-BIN-14; regex rules agree with CS-SEC-03; CA1867 none list agrees with CS-BUILD-12 and the shipped globalconfig; the retired IDs agree with binaries.md.

4. DELETION TEST
 - PERF-02's optional MA0110 sentence: measured with the line on, MA0110 fires on 6 of the 10 forms SYSLIB1045 already flags and on none of the TimeSpan forms the consolidation hoped it would close. Delete.
 - Failure-mode row 10 (params object[] / catch FormatException): the consolidation itself dropped both as common knowledge; the row has no rule ID. Delete or keep as a one-line bullet.
 - CS-PERF-01 mostly restates CS-CORE-01 (weaken list) and CS-BUILD-12 (NoWarn, none list); its unique content is G1 and the CA1805 `= default;` advice. Left as is, noted.

5. ERA + PORTABILITY
Version/date coverage is good (every measured claim dated 2026-10-11, TFM named, Windows rows say SDK 10.0.102, macOS/arm64 unverified). No ocx leak beyond labelled examples (OCX_HOME, .ocx, tests/Ocx.Sdk.UnitTests, the "example tool ocx.exe 0.5.7" line), no /home paths, no fixture names. One undated external: "until 0.16 is GA" (BenchmarkDotNet), minor, not filed. The claim "xargs exits 123 when a batch lists a file" is wrong (F6).

6. READING
House voice holds: imperative, tables, no hedging except PERF-07 "allocates nothing it can avoid" (vague, minor, not filed). Contents lines present, all 6 + 5 anchors resolve. Routing row for platform-and-paths in csharp-quality.md omits delays, timeouts and retries, working directory and splitting child output (F19, cross-unit).

All proposed regex fixes were run on the planted fixtures (fixes.sh): F1 prints 3, G6 fix leaves only the non-constant plant, G8 loose catches 4 of 4 planted loops and 0 on green, G9 loose catches F, G, H probes and 0 on green, G4 narrowed drops the ToLowerInvariant-output FP, G3 narrowed drops the indexer-initializer FP.

findings.problem: The Verification count cell cannot print 3 on the shipped posture: its three patterns end in `$` but the row itself requires, and analyzers.globalconfig carries, a trailing `# CS-PERF-02` on each line.
findings.evidence: Ran verbatim against a copy of rules/dotnet-build/checks/analyzers.globalconfig installed as .globalconfig: no output, exit 1. On a hand-stripped file (no trailing comment) it prints 3. Fixed patterns with `( #.*)?$` print 3 on the shipped file.
findings.fix: Replace the three `$` anchors with `( #.*)?$`, e.g. `rg -c -e '^dotnet_diagnostic\.SYSLIB1045\.severity = warning( #.*)?$' -e '^dotnet_code_quality\.CA1822\.api_surface = private, internal( #.*)?$' -e '^dotnet_diagnostic\.CA1867\.severity = none( #.*)?$' .globalconfig` prints `3`.

findings.problem: Procedure step 4's assertion (the only guard against exit-0 non-measurement) passes on a stale report: BenchmarkDotNet.Artifacts/results persists between runs, so a rerun that matches no benchmark still satisfies `test -n "$(ls ...-report-github.md)"`.
findings.evidence: Built a real benchmark project (BDN 0.15.8, net10.0). Run 1 with `--filter '*Pump*' --job dry` wrote PumpBench-report-github.md. Run 2 with `--filter '*NoSuchBench*'` exited 0 ("returned 0 benchmarks") and the assertion exited 0. After `rm -rf BenchmarkDotNet.Artifacts` before the run, the same no-match run leaves no report and the assertion exits 1.
findings.fix: Add before the run: `rm -rf benchmarks/Example.Benchmarks/BenchmarkDotNet.Artifacts`, and say the "watched red" covers a rerun with a non-matching filter, not only a first run.

findings.problem: G6 flags every stackalloc size that is not a bare digit literal, so named constants and constant expressions (which the rule allows) and the idiomatic `if (n <= Max) { stackalloc }` form go red; the rule text also demands the `<=` on the stackalloc line itself.
findings.evidence: Planted `stackalloc byte[MaxStack]` and `stackalloc byte[16 * 1024]` both hit. Held-out: 19 hits in opentelemetry-dotnet and grpc-dotnet, 13 are `const int` names (TraceIdSizeInBytes, Limit, MaxFreeSlotCandidates, StackallocByteThreshold, MaxFormattedDoubleCharacters x4, HeaderSize, MaxUnicodeCharsReallocate*MaxUtf8BytesPerUnicodeChar) and BaggagePropagator.cs:443 is guarded by `if (value.Length <= StackallocByteThreshold)` on the previous line.
findings.fix: Treat digits, PascalCase identifiers and + - * of them as constant: `rg -n -P '^(?!.*<=).*stackalloc\s+\w+\s*\[(?!\s*(?:\d+|[A-Z]\w*)(?:\s*[*+-]\s*(?:\d+|[A-Z]\w*))*\s*\])' --glob '*.cs' src` (verified: planted FPs gone, `stackalloc byte[n]` still hits). Reword the rule to "a constant size, or a `<=` guard on its line or the enclosing `if`".

findings.problem: G5 and the rule ("exactly one Return, inside finally") fail every legitimate ownership shape that real code uses, and G5 prints the whole Rent-to-Return span (107 lines for one hit).
findings.evidence: All 4 hit files in the held-out trees are valid: grpc Base64RequestStream.cs (buffer held in a field, returned in Dispose), grpc StreamExtensions.cs:71 to :112 (grow by Return then Rent, final Return in finally at :188), otel PooledList.cs (struct returned in Dispose), Newtonsoft DemoTests.cs (IArrayPool adapter whose Rent and Return are separate methods). 0 genuine violations; grpc output was 149 lines for 2 sites.
findings.fix: Add the carve-outs to the rule (a buffer owned by a field or struct and returned in Dispose; a grow-swap Return followed by Rent inside the same try; a thin adapter), keep G5 for locals, and make it print one line per site: `rg -U -P -n -o 'Shared\.Rent\((?=(?:(?!\bfinally\b)[\s\S])*?Shared\.Return\()' --glob '*.cs' src` (verified: 2 lines instead of 149).

findings.problem: CS-XP-04 resolves from a "non-empty" variable while CS-BIN-13 requires a rooted value and calls a relative one "the CS-XP-04 cwd hazard"; as written, a relative HOME, USERPROFILE or tool-home variable yields the cwd-relative root the rule exists to prevent.
findings.evidence: binaries.md CS-BIN-13: "A relative or empty variable counts as unset (the `CS-XP-04` cwd hazard)". platform-and-paths.md CS-XP-04: "a non-empty tool home variable ... a non-empty USERPROFILE or HOME". The unit's own measured example (HOME=/tmp/no-such-home giving a rooted False result) is the same hazard.
findings.fix: Say "non-empty and rooted (`Path.IsPathRooted`); a relative or empty value counts as unset" in all three tiers, and add a resolver unit-test row `HOME=rel` falling through to the next tier.

findings.problem: The Static Gate paragraph says every xargs exits 123 "when a batch lists a file"; it is the opposite: xargs exits 123 when the inner rg exits 1, i.e. when nothing is listed (the pass case).
findings.evidence: P1 and P2 on the planted green tree print nothing and PIPESTATUS is `0 123`; on the red tree they list the file and PIPESTATUS is `0 0`.
findings.fix: Write: "Every `xargs` here exits 123 when it lists nothing (the pass case) and 0 when it lists a file; read the output, not the status."

findings.problem: The InvariantGlobalization cell scans only `tests`, so a root or src Directory.Build.props that sets it (which applies to the test projects) is missed.
findings.evidence: xp-red has `<InvariantGlobalization>true</InvariantGlobalization>` in a root Directory.Build.props; the cell lists only tests/Ocx.Sdk.UnitTests/U.csproj (the planted test csproj). Removing that csproj leaves empty output. The runtime sweep would still throw, so this is a verification-cell gap, not a rule gap.
findings.fix: Scan from the root: `rg -l -g '*.csproj' -g '*.props' -g '*.targets' -e '\x3CInvariantGlobalization\x3E\s*true' .`, and add `-e 'GLOBALIZATION_INVARIANT'` for workflow files if the rule should cover the environment form.

findings.problem: The Split cell misses five common spellings and flags non-child text; the rule says "child text" but the check hits all of src.
findings.evidence:
Planted misses (no hit): `Split(new[] { '
' })`, `Split('', '
')`, `Split(new char[] { '', '
' }, ...)`, `Regex.Split(s, @"?
")`, `Split(["
", "
"], ...)`. Held-out FP: Newtonsoft JsonTextWriter.cs:800 `text.Split('
')` on the writer's own text.
findings.fix: Add `-e 'Split\(.*\\[rn]'` style alternatives (e.g. `-e 'Split\(.*\\n'`) and scope the sentence: "Split text that came from a child process"; note the check lists own-text sites for reading.

findings.problem: CS-XP-06 bans only `Directory.SetCurrentDirectory`; `Environment.CurrentDirectory = ...` (the form agents also write in test setup) builds green and no cell catches it.
findings.evidence: Shipped BannedSymbols.txt plus `Environment.CurrentDirectory = "/tmp"` builds exit 0 on both TFMs. A `M:System.Environment.set_CurrentDirectory(System.String)` ban line is silent; `P:System.Environment.CurrentDirectory` fires but also bans reads. `rg -n -g '*.cs' -e 'Environment\.CurrentDirectory\s*=[^=]' src tests` hits the plant.

findings.problem: The rule says every clock, delay and timeout takes the injected TimeProvider, but the ban set covers only DateTime/DateTimeOffset now-properties, Task.Delay, the CancellationTokenSource constructor, CancelAfter and Thread.Sleep.
findings.evidence: Built green with the shipped posture on both TFMs: `Task.WaitAsync(TimeSpan)`, `Task.WaitAsync(TimeSpan, CancellationToken)`, `new PeriodicTimer(...)`, `new Timer(...)`, `Stopwatch.GetTimestamp()`. CS-PROC-13 itself uses `t.WaitAsync(grace, timeProvider)`, so the provider form is the intended one.

findings.problem: P2 flags every P/Invoke file, but the rule only requires SupportedOSPlatform on types that import kernel32 or advapi32; a libc-only file prints, and the rule text omits other Windows DLLs the check does catch (ntdll, user32). The -windows TFM cell misses an attribute-conditioned TargetFramework.
findings.evidence: xp-libc: a file with only `[DllImport("libc")]` is listed by P2. Held-out: grpc Native.cs imports ntdll.dll and kernel32.dll and is rightly listed though the rule names only kernel32 or advapi32. xp-red src/c/Lib3.csproj `<TargetFramework Condition=...>net10.0-windows</TargetFramework>` is not matched by `\x3CTargetFrameworks?\x3E`.

findings.problem: The XP gate line and the PERF step 4 command do not follow DN-RULE-01 (timeout plus redirect to a file), DN-RULE-02 / CS-BUILD-30 (`--tl:off --interactive false`) or DN-RULE-10 (`--disable-build-servers`), the form async.md and binaries.md use.
findings.evidence: platform-and-paths.md:34 is `dotnet build --no-incremental`; performance.md step 4 is `dotnet run -c Release --project ... -- --filter ... --job short -m`. csharp-quality.md DN-RULE-01 (MUST) and async.md:35 show `timeout 900 dotnet build --tl:off --interactive false --disable-build-servers -nologo -v:q --no-incremental > build.log 2>&1; echo $?`.
findings.fix: Use the DN-RULE-01 form for the build gate; for the BDN run use `timeout 1800 dotnet run -c Release --project ... > bench.log 2>&1` and read bench.log.

findings.problem: The rule says every literal-pattern regex is anchored `\A` to `\z`; the consolidation (and CS-BIN-08) require that only for validating patterns. Anchoring a search, Replace or Split pattern changes its behaviour.
findings.evidence: csharp-performance.md rule text has no anchor clause; the anchor appears only under "Do not copy from Python" for `^...$` validators and CS-BIN-08 (manifest validators). performance.md CS-PERF-03 puts it on every literal regex.
findings.fix: Write "a validating pattern is anchored `\A`..`\z` (CS-BIN-08)" and drop the clause from the general sentence.

findings.problem: G8 needs the loop to follow the declaration with nothing between and a brace-free `+=` body; most real forms are missed. G9 (candidate list) misses any loop header containing a call or any LINQ after a nested brace, and prints multi-line spans.
findings.evidence: Planted misses for G8: extra statement before the loop, `if { s += x; }` inside the loop, `s = s + x`. Held-out: Azure__bicep ExpressionHelpers.cs:32 missed by G8 while Bogus UserAgentGenerator.cs:56 hits. G9 planted misses: `foreach (var x in xs.Where(...)) { ... xs.Count(...) }`, LINQ inside `if { }`, `foreach (var x in Get(xs))`; it hit only the flat one-line body.

findings.problem: G3 matches index initializers and G4 matches case normalisation on the output side of a comparison.
findings.evidence: Planted `new() { ["a"] = 1, ["b"] = 2 }` hits G3 via `, ["b"]`; planted `if (s.StartsWith("x", Ordinal)) return s.ToLowerInvariant();` hits G4 because `[^;]*` spans the closing paren. Narrowed G3 (`(?![^\]]*\]\s*=)`) and G4 (`[^;)]*`) drop those hits and keep the 3 genuine G4 plants and the loop collection-expression plant.
findings.fix: G3: `rg -n -P '[(,]\s*\[\s*["\x27\d-](?![^\]]*\]\s*=)' --glob '*.cs' src`. G4: replace `[^;]*` with `[^;)]*` in the first alternative.

findings.problem: G2 misses three forms of the rule's banned constructs, and G11 misses the wording agents use for a perf claim.
findings.evidence: G2 planted misses: `new System.Text.RegularExpressions.Regex(...)`, `static Regex G { get; } = new(...)`, `new Regex ("x")`. G11 planted dodges: a commit "perf: lower allocation count in the pump" and "perf: avoid a copy; 3x quicker" print nothing; the `perf:` type itself is not a trigger.
findings.fix: G2: add `-e 'Regex\.Regex\('`-style alternatives `new\s+(?:[\w.]+\.)?Regex\s*\(` and `Regex\s+\w+\s*\{[^}]*\}\s*=\s*new\s*\(`. G11: add `-e '^perf'`, `-e 'quicker'`, `-e 'lower alloc'`.

findings.problem: G10 flags code that is not a rewrite for speed (the rule's subject) and multi-line static readonly declarations.
findings.evidence: opentelemetry-dotnet: 10 hits; Metric.cs:48 and :71 are continuation lines of `static readonly` declarations (FP); the rest are per-provider FrozenSets built once and read per measurement (instance fields, a method return), which the rule text would only forbid as a speed rewrite. The cell's own note admits the one-line limit.
findings.fix: Say G10 is a candidate list for added Frozen conversions in the diff (run it on `git diff` added lines), or accept `static readonly` on the previous line with `-B1`.

findings.problem: The sentence offering `MA0110` as an optional fourth line contradicts "exactly three", is moot because Meziantou is in the posture, and adds no coverage over SYSLIB1045.
findings.evidence: With `dotnet_diagnostic.MA0110.severity = warning` added to a build with the shipped posture, MA0110 fired on 6 of the 10 Regex forms SYSLIB1045 already flags (and RS0030 bans) and on none of the TimeSpan forms; the consolidation's premise that it closes the timeout gap is false.

findings.problem: Failure-mode row 10 (params object[] helpers, int.Parse wrapped in catch FormatException) is common knowledge the consolidation itself dropped as a rule; it has no rule ID and its two greps are hit-or-miss reading aids.
findings.evidence: csharp-performance.md Verdict 10: "Dropped as common knowledge ... Try* instead of catching FormatException, params object[]". The table row's Check column cites no ID.

findings.problem: The index routing row for platform-and-paths.md names paths, home, file names, number formatting, Windows-only APIs, platform and clock, but not delays, timeouts and retries, the working directory or splitting child output, which are the subjects of CS-XP-11, CS-XP-06 and CS-XP-12.

reviews.trigger_eval: n/a for load behaviour: both files carry a never-matching paths glob (**/.csharp-quality-depth-on-demand) by design and load only through the index routing rows at csharp-quality.md:147 and :152.
